children: Shares of commercial real estate lender Ladder Capital

jumped 3.9% in the afternoon session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 financial results. According to the company's release, GAAP income before taxes was $67.3 million, or $0.53 a share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30. Distributable earnings were $44.7 million, or $0.35 a share, and $0.38 a share before a credit-loss charge-off. Chief executive Brian Harris said Ladder made more than $700 million of new loan and securities investments, grew book value, and recorded a gain on the sale of a net-lease office asset. He said the balance sheet is set up to benefit from higher rates. On the call, president Pamela McCormack said the sale of the Jacksonville office campus added $31 million to distributable earnings and earned an 18% return over the life of the investment.

The property sold above its carrying value, and undepreciated book value rose to $13.50 a share from $13.44. Of the new investments, $481 million went into mostly AAA securities and $222 million into seven new loans, after higher rates slowed lending in September. Chief financial officer Paul said 57% of the debt is fixed-rate, at a 5.3% average coupon, while 92% of interest-earning assets float. Each quarter-point increase in the secured overnight financing rate adds about one cent a share to quarterly distributable earnings.
The shares were trading at $9.19, up 3.9% from the previous close.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Ladder Capital’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 1 move greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was about 23 hours ago when the stock gained 3.2% on the news that Mortgage lenders rose as Treasury yields fell and investors moved into government bonds. According to CNBC, the 10-year yield dropped more than 9 basis points to 5.093%, the 30-year fell more than 9 basis points to 5.425%, and the 2-year fell more than 4 basis points to 4.759%. CNBC tied the move to a flight out of technology shares and into bonds. Wholesale prices rose 6.3% in September from a year earlier, the biggest gain since 2022 and above the 5.5% Dow Jones estimate. That followed Wednesday’s consumer-price report, which showed prices up 3.7% on the year. Investors sold high-flying technology stocks on concern that hotter inflation and higher rates would pressure spending on artificial intelligence, and that selling pushed money into Treasuries. The 10-year yield is the benchmark for home loans. A lower yield cuts funding costs for originators and can bring back purchase and refinance demand. That is the setup that lifted Rocket Companies and the other mortgage and real-estate finance names in the group.

Ladder Capital is down 17.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $9.19 per share, it is trading 19.6% below its 52-week high of $11.42 from December 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Ladder Capital’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $769.26.
